pr.title: Add an intrinsic for `ptr::from_raw_parts(_mut)`
pr.description:
Fixes #123174 
cc @CAD97 @saethlin 
r? @cjgillot 

As suggested in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/123190#issuecomment-2028717967, this adds a new `AggregateKind::RawPtr` for creating a pointer from its data pointer and its metadata.

That means that `slice::from_raw_parts` and friends no longer need to hard-code pointer layout into `libcore`, and because it no longer does union hacks the MIR is shorter and more amenable to optimizations.
pr.author: scottmcm

issues.title: UB Check blocks MIR inlining of `Vec::deref`
issues.body:
### Code I tried this code: [[playground]](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=release&edition=2021&gist=6375eea58c531afdd6dfd4be1563858b) ```rust pub fn closed(v: &Vec) -> &[u8] { v } pub fn open(v: &Vec) -> &[u8] { vec_deref(v) } #[inline] fn vec_deref(v: &Vec) -> &[T] { unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(v.as_ptr(), v.len()) } } ``` I expected to see this happen: in release mode with default MIR optimization, both `closed` and `open` would generate equivalent optimized MIR — an inlined conversion from `&Vec` to `&[u8]` (deconstruct the `Vec` into ptr and len then build the `&[_]`). Instead, this happened: On 1.77.0, the inlining happens as expected. On 1.78.0-beta.3 (2024-03-27 4147533e05ee20c4fcc4), ` as Deref>::deref` (`vec_deref` for `open`) is called outline. Impactfully, the call is additionally not known to never unwind (`-> [return: …, unwind continue]` in MIR), which likely impedes optimization around the call.

_7 = std::slice::from_raw_parts::precondition_check(move _8, move _9, move _10, _3) -> [return: bb2, unwind unreachable]; } bb2: { StorageDead(_10); StorageDead(_9); StorageDead(_8); goto -> bb3; } bb3: { StorageDead(_6); StorageLive(_12); _12 = _2 as *const () (PtrToPtr); StorageLive(_13); StorageLive(_14); _14 = std::ptr::metadata::PtrComponents::<[T]> { data_pointer: _12, metadata: _3 }; _13 = std::ptr::metadata::PtrRepr::<[T]> { const_ptr: move _14 }; StorageDead(_14); _11 = (_13.0: *const [T]); StorageDead(_13); StorageDead(_12); _0 = &(*_11); StorageDead(_3); StorageDead(_2); return; } } ``` -----
On stable, `vec_deref`'s optimized MIR is a single straightline basic block. On beta, it contains a `switchInt` on `UbCheck(LanguageUb)` guarding a conditional call to `std::slice::from_raw_parts::precondition_check`, resulting in four basic blocks including an MIR call operation. AIUI both of these metrics (block/call count) directly contribute to the MIR inlining heuristics.
stable slice::from_raw_parts ```rust pub const unsafe fn from_raw_parts<'a, T>(data: *const T, len: usize) -> &'a [T] { // SAFETY: the caller must uphold the safety contract for `from_raw_parts`. unsafe { assert_unsafe_precondition!( "slice::from_raw_parts requires the pointer to be aligned and non-null, and the total size of the slice not to exceed `isize::MAX`", [T](data: *const T, len: usize) => is_aligned_and_not_null(data) && is_valid_allocation_size::(len) ); &*ptr::slice_from_raw_parts(data, len) } } ``` -----
beta slice::from_raw_parts ```rust pub const unsafe fn from_raw_parts<'a, T>(data: *const T, len: usize) -> &'a [T] { // SAFETY: the caller must uphold the safety contract for `from_raw_parts`. unsafe { assert_unsafe_precondition!( check_language_ub, "slice::from_raw_parts requires the pointer to be aligned and non-null, and the total size of the slice not to exceed `isize::MAX`", ( data: *mut () = data as *mut (), size: usize = size_of::(), align: usize = align_of::(), len: usize = len, ) => is_aligned_and_not_null(data, align) && is_valid_allocation_size(size, len) ); &*ptr::slice_from_raw_parts(data, len) } } ``` -----
### Version it worked on It most recently worked on: Rust Stable 1.77.0 ### Version with regression It isn't working on: Rust Beta 1.78.0-beta.3 (2024-03-27 4147533e05ee20c4fcc4) ### Meta Found [on irlo](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/pre-acp-un-specialize-impl-tostring/20549/4?u=cad97) while looking at inlining behavior of `ToString`. @rustbot modify labels: +regression-from-stable-to-beta (didn't do `-regression-untriaged` since I didn't try to narrow it any further than playground stable/beta, but don't know the convention here) cc @saethlin (IIRC you've been working on `assert_unsafe_precondition!`s and other `precondition_check`s)

processing.reason:
The PR only ever implements the guarded rewrite: InstSimplify rewrites `Aggregate(RawPtr, [data, meta])` to `Cast(PtrToPtr, data)` solely when `meta_ty.is_unit()`, i.e., for thin pointers. For fat pointers (non-unit metadata such as a slice length) it leaves the RawPtr aggregate intact, so metadata is preserved. The frozen analysis itself states that the unguarded over-broad rewrite was never executed or reproduced historically; it is only the semantic boundary the guard must respect.

Any source-level pair attempting to model the unguarded rewrite would have to fabricate the behavior of discarding non-unit metadata (for example by forcing a slice length to 0), because faithfully casting a thin data pointer to a fat slice pointer is not a well-defined ordinary-Rust operation. That would be manufacturing an arbitrary return-value change rather than encoding an actual historical wrong transformation, which the task forbids. Since the historically implemented transformation is correctly guarded and no source-grounded original/incorrect pair exists for this PR head, no valid counterexample can be produced.

analysis.summary: PR adds the `aggregate_raw_ptr` intrinsic, lowers it in LowerIntrinsics to `Rvalue::Aggregate(AggregateKind::RawPtr(pointee_ty, mutability), [data, meta])`, and teaches InstSimplify to rewrite the thin-pointer case (`meta` has unit type) into a `CastKind::PtrToPtr` cast. Fat-pointer aggregates (non-unit metadata such as slice length) must remain aggregates.
analysis.originalLogic: LowerIntrinsics replaces `aggregate_raw_ptr::<P, D, M>(data, meta)` with a two-field `Rvalue::Aggregate` whose kind is `AggregateKind::RawPtr`, derived from the intrinsic return type: `let kind = if let ty::RawPtr(pointee_ty, mutability) = pointer_ty.kind() { AggregateKind::RawPtr(*pointee_ty, *mutability) }`. The aggregate documentation requires both operands always: a raw data pointer of matching mutability with a thin pointee, plus the appropriate `Pointee::Metadata` value, using unit metadata for thin pointers. InstSimplify's original logic leaves the aggregate in place; the newly added logic inspects `fields.raw[1].ty(...)` and only rewrites when that metadata type is unit.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The bounded transformation under test is `Aggregate(RawPtr, [p, ()]) -> Cast(PtrToPtr, p)`. This is correct only with the `meta_ty.is_unit()` guard. An unguarded form that always replaces a RawPtr aggregate with a PtrToPtr cast would incorrectly discard non-unit metadata (for example a slice length), changing a fat pointer's metadata rather than just casting a thin data pointer. No such over-broad rewrite is claimed to have been executed or reproduced historically; it is the semantic boundary the pass must respect.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR after intrinsic lowering containing `Rvalue::Aggregate(AggregateKind::RawPtr(pointee_ty, mutability), [data, meta])`. Thin-pointer cases have `meta: ()` and may be simplified. Fat-pointer cases have non-unit metadata such as `usize` for slices and must not be simplified. Both const and mut pointers are in scope; the pointer type is built from the aggregate's pointee type and mutability.
analysis.trigger: LowerIntrinsics encounters a call to `aggregate_raw_ptr`, requires exactly two arguments and a raw-pointer return type, emits the RawPtr aggregate, and rewrites the terminator to a Goto. InstSimplify then fires on a RawPtr aggregate only when the second field's type is unit.
preconditions: LowerIntrinsics requires exactly two operands: `let Ok([data, meta]) = <[_; 2]>::try_from(std::mem::take(args))`
LowerIntrinsics requires the intrinsic return type to be a raw pointer before forming `AggregateKind::RawPtr`
The RawPtr aggregate has exactly two fields: a raw data pointer with matching mutability and a thin pointee, plus a metadata value
InstSimplify may rewrite only when the second operand's type is unit, i.e. `if meta_ty.is_unit()`
The replacement cast must use the aggregate's `pointee_ty` and `mutability` to form the destination pointer type
pitfalls: Do not simplify fat-pointer RawPtr aggregates: dropping a non-unit metadata operand would lose slice length or other pointee metadata
Do not use `is_zst` as the simplification guard; the implemented condition is specifically the unit metadata type

Do not assume every RawPtr aggregate produces a pointer Pair; codegen treats the unit-metadata case as Immediate/ZeroSized, and interpretation handles it separately rather than via normal field projection
The transform replaces the whole rvalue with `Rvalue::Cast(CastKind::PtrToPtr, data, ptr_ty)` using the aggregate kind's pointee type and mutability, not an arbitrary target pointer type
InstSimplify is gated by `consider_optimizing`, so absence of the rewrite is not itself a correctness failure
Panic strategy does not change this lowering: the abort and unwind LowerIntrinsics diffs are identical
analysis.testStrategy: Use a MIR-pass test for InstSimplify (`//@ test-mir-pass: InstSimplify`, `#![feature(core_intrinsics)]`) that calls `std::intrinsics::aggregate_raw_ptr(x, ())` and checks the output contains `_0 = move _2 as *const () (PtrToPtr);` as in `cast_thin_via_aggregate`. Pair it with a non-unit-metadata program (for example `aggregate_raw_ptr(data, len)` producing a slice pointer) that must retain the RawPtr aggregate. Use a LowerIntrinsics `// EMIT_MIR ... .diff` test like `make_pointers` covering `*const i32`, `*mut u8`, `*const [u16]`, and `*mut [u64]` to verify the intrinsic becomes `*const i32 from (move _5, move _6)` etc. and the terminator becomes `goto`. Run under both panic strategies as the tests use `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`. These two programs differ only in the metadata operand type, isolating the InstSimplify guard.
